transcript.text: Hey, so this is the review? I think it's been a decent year, honestly, given everything.

Thanks for coming in, Marcus. I want to be straightforward with you: your overall rating this year is Below Expectations, and that's final following calibration. The main reasons are that you reached 61% of your renewal target when the team average was 94%, and both Helix and Orbis escalated concerns about missed follow-ups, once in March and again in June. I know that's hard to hear, so I'd like to hear your view, and then talk about a 90-day development plan to turn this around.

Below Expectations? Wait, hold on. 61%? Half my book got reassigned in Q2 when the acquisition happened, and nobody seems to have accounted for that. Vantage and Corvel just vanished off my territory overnight. How is that on me?

That's a fair point, and I did take the Q2 reassignment into account, but even looking at the accounts you kept, the follow-up gaps with Helix and Orbis were within your control, and we talked about them in our 1:1s in April and July. The rating is final, so I can't change it, but I'd like to understand what got in the way of those follow-ups. Can you walk me through what was happening there?

Okay... yeah, I'll be straight with you. Helix and Orbis got hit with the reassignment at the same time, and I was rebuilding my whole pipeline from scratch. Some of the follow-ups just slipped, and I kept telling myself I'd catch up. I didn't.

I appreciate you being honest about that, Marcus, it helps me a lot. Rebuilding a pipeline while carrying live accounts is a hard spot, and I'd rather we fix the system than just say try harder. So for the 90-day plan, I'd like to build in a simple follow-up tracking routine and a regular check-in with me, and I'd like your input on what support would actually make a difference. What do you think would help most?

Honestly? A tracking system would help, but I think the bigger thing was that nobody told me which accounts were officially mine after the handoff. I was guessing for weeks. If I knew exactly what I owned, I'd have been way less scattered.

That's useful to know, Marcus, and I'm sorry the handoff left you guessing for weeks. Let's make the first step of the plan a written list of exactly which accounts you own, confirmed between us, so there's no ambiguity going forward. Alongside that, we'll set up the follow-up tracker and a regular check-in, and I'd like you to draft how you want the tracker to work so it fits the way you actually run your accounts. Does that sound workable to you?

Yeah, that works. A written list of what's mine would've saved me a lot of guessing. I'm still not thrilled the rating's final, though. Can I at least see the numbers for the accounts I actually kept, so I know what I'm being measured against?

Yes, I can share those, and I understand why you want to see them, since you should know exactly what you're measured against. I'll pull together the target and results for the accounts you kept so we can go through them side by side. One more thing I haven't covered yet: there's no pay rise this cycle, but you stay bonus-eligible next year, so the 90-day plan matters for that too.

Okay, that's fair, I'll take the numbers. Bonus eligibility helps, I guess, but no raise stings when I'm already sitting on a Below. Can you make sure the account list includes Vantage and Corvel, or at least shows they're off my books? I don't want to be measured on them.
